This means I had been passed once already, or does it? Davies's time was 7.16. You can work out what mine would have been for the full stretch (assuming I'd get there at all) yourself.

The result gives that fillip to Club prestige badly needed at this time and even encourages us to think that next October we may even lead the field with the help of Davies, Hallowell and Newell, to mention names which readily come to mind.

In the 4 x 440 yards our team of Alan Sexton, Jackson, Davies and Morris were third in their heat and did not qualify for the final according to placing, but imagine their surprise when they learned that they had in fact qualified as the fastest losers, and they eventually finished 4th in the final.

Experience has been given to newcomers to this event, which will help us next April, and now that S.L.H. have lost the great Gordon and we can improve on our team by the inclusion of Davies and Hallowell, it can be hoped that last year's 5th position in the National Relay can be bettered by at least 4 places.

Davies, Newell and Hallowell led the field after an early dash by Frank Wright. For some unaccountable reason Davies almost stopped with three laps to go and so the race became a duel between Newell and Hallowell.
The next leg was a new one of little more than two miles in length and John Davies, complete with an arm in plaster following a fracture, was entrusted with it.

Good times were recorded by Baulch, Bhatia, Davies and Newell. These two races,followed by our own 5¾ miles road race and 3 miles yacht handicap, preceded the London to Brighton Relay for Southern clubs on October 11th and we had every reason to think we were set for a place - in actual fact we had…

Beware; Davies, Bhatia and Robinson!! The field events boys were out in force and both Percy Porter and Dave Ansell won their respective events - the hammer, with 158'10½", and the long-jump with a leap of 20'5½".

Eric was still 8th and Alan now 12th fighting it out with Davies (TVH) and Paxton (HHH). Bob Glover was fading badly and was now a further 1½ mins. down, having been caught by Joe Dooley and Bob Plummer.

Normally our middle-distance men could have split forces but on this occasion we had Newell, Robinson, Dabbs and Radford on holiday, Davies injured and Bhatia a 'flu victim; so it was decided to concentrate our remaining forces on the only major road-relay event we tackle before the "Brighton".

We need some new blood so before April let us see some form from such people as Miller, Thresher, Linstead, Johnston, Stearman, and a return to the team by Hallowell, Davies and Baulch (not new blood but almost indispensable).

South London had five of the first six in the 3,000 metres event, but with only two to score Davies (8:54.4) and Black (9:11.6) were able to total 10 pts against the 15 of SLH, and thus kept our noses well to the front.
Kerr, Newell, Davies, Walker, Black, Dabbs, Linstead, Maclean. How's that for a line up to set a new 3 mile record?
Sandwiched between Black and Forey the four runners on "trial" were Davies, Dabbs, Thresher, and Miller. The two Johns won the day, but there was little else of interest to Belgrave.

Our scoring trio of Mann, O'Connor and Piotrowski only managed to pull back Davies, Franklin and Whitley of Thames Valley over the last two miles of the race.

The first of the short stages saw John setting off with Davies (TVH) haring after him. The "Valley" man swept past and went on to clock the fastest short stage time of the day but John was not put off in the slightest and brought us to the next take-over 23 seconds ahead of Hillingdon, now 3rd, and…
What a fine season JOHN BICOURT has been having. Now established as an international choice, John has only had Hollings and Davies to contend with amongst U.K.
At Johannesburg (6,500ft) he clocked 9:09.4 behind Bonzet (S.A) 8:56.8 and Davies (TVH/GB) 9:04.8, and at Pretoria (4,000ft) these three repeated their placings with 8:56.0, 8:57.6, 9:01.8.
Of course anything could happen and with rivals of the calibre of Davies, Staynings and Coates he will have to be in top form to make the team but he has plenty of determination.

Behind Ernie were top rated British sprinters Green, Hoyte and Roberts plus Davies of Jamaica. These performances added to Carl Lawton's fourth place in the 10km walk back in March give Belgrave a highly creditable 2nd and four 4ths for 1977.
